extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and Technology Center (TC) directors
extracted.subtask_description: Instructions and required form-paragraph wording for USPTO examiners to use when making 35 U.S.C. 101 subject-matter-eligibility rejections under the 2019 Revised Patent Subject Matter Eligibility Guidance (2019 PEG).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 2019 PEG procedure for Step 1 vs Step 2B
rubrics_metrics.description: Differentiate rejections under Step 1 (claim not to a statutory category) versus Step 2B (claim directed to a judicial exception without an inventive concept/significantly more) and use the specified form paragraphs accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Step 1 rejections based on failure to claim an invention that falls within the statutory categories (not a process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter), continue to use form paragraphs 7.04.01, 7.05 and 7.05.01. For Step 2B rejections based on a claim directed to a judicial exception without providing an inventive concept/significantly more, use form paragraphs 7.04.01, 7.05 and the new form paragraph(s): 7.05.016 (for enumerated abstract ideas, laws of nature, natural phenomena) and 7.05.016 together with 7.05.017 (for non-enumerated abstract ideas, because TC Director approval is required).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.04.01 — Statement of Statutory Basis (preceding use of 35 U.S.C. 101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the statutory text of 35 U.S.C. 101 and precede the first use of 35 U.S.C. 101 in all first actions on the merits and final rejections with this form paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This form paragraph must precede the first use of 35 U.S.C. 101 in all first actions on the merits and final rejections. It contains the statutory language: 'Whoever invents or discovers any new and useful process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter ...' (use exact statutory text provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.05 — Rejection Heading and Required Follow-up
rubrics_metrics.description: Use form paragraph 7.05 as the rejection heading for 35 U.S.C. 101 rejections and follow it with detailed explanation form paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.05 is a heading-only paragraph: 'Claim [1] rejected under 35 U.S.C. 101 because'. Examiner notes: (1) must be preceded by 7.04.01 in first actions and final rejections; (2) must be followed by a detailed explanation of the grounds of rejection using one or more of form paragraphs 7.05.01, 7.05.016, 7.05.02, 7.05.03, or another appropriate reason; (3) see MPEP §§ 2105 - 2107.03 for additional guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.05.01 — Nonstatutory (Not One of the Four Statutory Categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the claimed invention is directed to nonstatutory subject matter (does not fall into process, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter), use 7.05.01 and explain why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 7.05.01 preceded by 7.05. In bracket 1, explain why the claimed invention is not patent eligible by identifying what the claim is directed to and why it does not fall within the four categories (examples: 'signal per se', 'mere information in the form of data', 'a contract', or 'a human being' — see MPEP § 2106,I). If a claim is directed to a judicial exception and is nonstatutory, use form paragraph 7.05.016 instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.05.016 — Nonstatutory (Directed to a Judicial Exception without an Inventive Concept/Significantly More)
rubrics_metrics.description: For claims directed to a judicial exception (law of nature, natural phenomenon, or abstract idea) that do not include significantly more, use 7.05.016 to describe the exception, why it is an exception, why it is not integrated into a practical application, and why additional elements do not add significantly more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 7.05.016 preceded by 7.05. This paragraph is for use with all product (machine, manufacture, composition) and process claims. Fill brackets as follows: (1) bracket 1 — identify whether the claim(s) are directed to a law of nature, a natural phenomenon, or an abstract idea; (2) bracket 2 — identify the exception by referring to how it is recited in the claim and explain why it is considered an exception (e.g., refer to the enumerated abstract idea grouping in Section I of the 2019 PEG and give examples such as 'the Arrhenius equation...' or 'series of steps instructing how to hedge risk...'); for products of nature explain lack of marked difference (e.g., 'naturally occurring DNA segment ... not markedly different'); (3) bracket 3 — explain why the exception is not integrated into a practical application (examples: generic computer elements merely implementing the abstract idea; data gathering steps are insignificant extra-solution activity; placing a product of nature into a generic container like a test tube is a nominal or token extrasolution component); (4) bracket 4 — identify additional elements and explain why, separately and in combination, they do not add significantly more (an 'inventive concept') — e.g., storing and retrieving information in memory are well-understood, routine, conventional computer functions as recognized by court decisions listed in MPEP § 2106.05(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to accompany 7.05.016 with 7.05.017 for non-enumerated abstract ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: If the recited abstract idea does not fall within the enumerated groupings of abstract ideas in the 2019 PEG, 7.05.016 should be accompanied by 7.05.017 because TC Director approval is required to treat a non-enumerated limitation as an abstract idea.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner Note: For claims that recite a limitation that does not fall within the enumerated groupings of abstract ideas, 7.05.016 should be accompanied by 7.05.017. 7.05.016 alone may be used for enumerated abstract ideas, laws of nature, and natural phenomena; for non-enumerated abstract ideas, TC Director approval is required and must be documented with 7.05.017.

rubrics_metrics.name: ¶ 7.05.017 — TC Director Approval for Non-Enumerated Abstract Idea
rubrics_metrics.description: When treating a tentative/non-enumerated claim limitation as an abstract idea, obtain TC Director approval and use 7.05.017 to document the justification and signature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.05.017 must be preceded by 7.05.016. Use it to state that the identified claim limitation(s) does/does not fall within the enumerated groupings in Section I of the 2019 PEG but are being treated as an abstract idea, and provide the justification in bracket 1. The rejection must include the TC Director's signature in bracket 2 to evidence approval. Examiner Note: approval from the TC Director is required to treat a tentative abstract idea as an abstract idea. In bracket 1 provide justification (for example, explain why the limitation is among the 'basic tools of scientific and technological work').

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain integration into a practical application and when additional elements are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: When asserting that a claim is not integrated into a practical application, specifically explain why additional elements fail to meaningfully limit the judicial exception and why they do not add significantly more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide concrete explanations: e.g., generically recited computer elements 'do not add a meaningful limitation' because they merely implement the abstract idea on a computer; data-gathering steps required to use a naturally occurring correlation are 'insignificant extra-solution activity'; placing a product of nature into a generic container (test tube) is a token extra-solution component. For additional elements, explain why they, separately and in combination, do not amount to an 'inventive concept' (examples: storing and retrieving information in memory are routine and conventional). Reference court decisions listed in MPEP § 2106.05(d) where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of use — applicability to all claim types and exclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: 7.05.016 applies to all product and process claims directed to judicial exceptions; existing procedures for claims directed to or encompassing a human organism or limited by the Atomic Energy Act remain unchanged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 7.05.016 is for use with all product (machine, manufacture, composition of matter) and process claims, and for all claims directed to a law of nature, natural phenomenon, or abstract idea. No changes have been made to form paragraphs for rejections based on a claim directed to or encompassing a human organism or to procedures limited by the Atomic Energy Act — continue to follow MPEP §§ 706.03(a)(II) and 706.03(b) for such claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph procedural/administrative notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Administrative requirements for availability, modification, and signature when using the new form paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New form paragraphs 7.05.016 and 7.05.017 will be made available in OACS and OC. Examiner notes accompanying form paragraphs 7.05 and 7.05.01 are being modified to provide instructions for proper use of the new paragraphs. A TC Director's signature is required when form paragraph 7.05.017 is used; see the examiner notes accompanying 7.05.017.
